hints.title: Lexicographical Comparison Obstacle
hints.text: Deriving an alphabet ordering from a sorted dictionary requires comparing adjacent words to discover precedence pairs. How can pairwise character relations sequence unique symbols while spotting prefix violations or cycles?

hints.title: Prefix Order and Precedence Invariant
hints.text: Adjacent word comparison isolates the first differing character as a directed precedence rule. An earlier word cannot be strictly longer than a subsequent word if it matches its full prefix.

hints.title: Topological Character Order Procedure
hints.text: Build a directed graph for all unique characters by inspecting the first differing letter between adjacent words. Tally incoming edges. Process characters with zero incoming edges, decrementing outgoing targets. If all unique characters are processed, return the joined string, else return an empty string.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: C: total length of all words combined
U: number of unique characters (at most 26)
complexity.notes: Prefix checking and edge generation scan words once; topological sort processes at most 26 vertices.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all character permutations takes 26! which is impossible.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Adjacency set and indegree hash maps occupy constant bounded space for lowercase letters.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling the invalid prefix case (e.g. ['abc', 'ab']) and cycle detection.
